abstract: Post-cardiac injury syndrome (PCIS) is an inflammatory pleuropericardial syndrome that may follow myocardial, pericardial, or iatrogenic cardiac injury. Although pericardial effusion is a recognized complication of left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO), recurrent pleuropericardial inflammation after LAAO is less commonly described. We report a patient with persistent atrial fibrillation who underwent uncomplicated LAAO with a 28-mm Amplatzer Amulet device (Abbott Medical, Plymouth, MN, USA) following a recent hemorrhagic stroke. Post-implantation transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated appropriate device positioning without peridevice leak or pericardial effusion. Within two weeks, the patient developed chest pain, dyspnea, electrocardiographic ST-segment elevations, markedly elevated CRP, and a large hemorrhagic pericardial effusion with tamponade requiring drainage of 780 mL of frank blood. The subsequent course was characterized by recurrent unilateral left exudative pleural effusions requiring repeated thoracenteses and chest tube drainage, followed by recurrence of both pleural and pericardial effusions. Serial microbiologic and cytologic studies were negative, and imaging demonstrated no evidence of malignancy. Colchicine was discontinued following an interval hospitalization, after which pleuropericardial effusions and systemic inflammation recurred. Following pleural drainage and reinitiation of colchicine, CRP declined from 87.8 mg/L (<8 mg/L) to 22.5 mg/L (<8 mg/L), respiratory symptoms resolved, and the patient was discharged home on room air. The temporal relationship to LAAO, recurrent pleuropericardial involvement, inflammatory response, exclusion of alternative etiologies, and clinical course were consistent with PCIS. This case highlights PCIS as an important consideration in patients presenting with recurrent pleural or pericardial effusions after LAAO while emphasizing the need to exclude mechanical device complications.
title: Recurrent Pleuropericardial Effusions Following Amplatzer Amulet Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: A Case of Post-Cardiac Injury Syndrome.

abstract: Reperfusion therapy has transformed acute ischemic stroke care, yet large-vessel recanalization does not ensure capillary reperfusion, preservation of the blood-brain barrier and neurovascular unit (BBB/NVU), or durable neurological recovery. Nanomedicine is still commonly judged by BBB crossing or ischemic-hemisphere accumulation, although vascular access, tissue viability, transport phenotype, thromboinflammation, and standard treatment change rapidly during the lifetime of a formulation. This narrative review proposes a conceptual framework that matches the reperfusion state and pathological interface to the compartment in which the therapeutically active entity must act. The framework is intended to organize preclinical evidence and generate testable translational hypotheses; it has not yet been clinically validated. Persistent occlusion may favor intravascular targets, whereas recanalization with no-reflow creates a distinct microvascular delivery problem. Early reperfusion injury may prioritize BBB/NVU stabilization, while later biological contexts may require selective immune, regenerative, or organelle-directed interventions. These contexts may coexist spatially, vary across vascular territories, and shift during treatment; they should therefore not be interpreted as a mandatory chronological sequence. We distinguish BBB crossing, controlled barrier modulation, and BBB/NVU repair as separate therapeutic tasks, and introduce transport attrition as a practical explanation for why sequential targeting, transcytosis, cellular uptake, endosomal escape, and organelle localization can yield little final active-entity exposure despite strong tissue imaging. Recent predominantly preclinical examples illustrate how thrombus-targeted rtPA systems, neutrophil-intercepting particles, NET-degrading polymersomes, lesion-targeted nanoplatforms, and mitochondrial nanomedicines may fit different delivery topologies. Translational credibility requires topology-resolved exposure, target engagement in viable tissue, hemocompatibility under antithrombotic treatment, state-appropriate models, function-linked manufacturing controls, and compatibility with thrombolysis and thrombectomy.
title: Beyond Blood-Brain Barrier Crossing in Reperfusion-Era Ischemic Stroke: Interface-Matched Active-Entity Delivery and Translational Product Design.

abstract: High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) complicated by cardiac arrest carries an extremely high mortality, and the optimal rescue strategy after an inadequate response to systemic thrombolysis remains uncertain. We report the case of a 53-year-old woman with previous deep-vein thrombosis who was admitted after an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest and subsequently experienced three additional episodes of cardiac arrest with pulseless electrical activity. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography demonstrated extensive bilateral central PE with severe right ventricular dilation and interventricular septal shift. Systemic thrombolysis with alteplase was administered. Despite thrombolysis and vasopressor/inotropic support, persistent cardiogenic-obstructive shock, electrical instability, and severe right ventricular pressure overload remained. Approximately 4 h after thrombolysis, rescue mechanical aspiration thrombectomy was performed using the Indigo® Aspiration System with Lightning Flash™ (Penumbra, Inc., Alameda, CA, USA). Ultrasound-guided right common femoral venous access was obtained with an 18 F sheath, and aspiration was performed in both pulmonary arteries. Pulmonary artery pressure decreased from 34 mmHg before aspiration to 25 mmHg at the end of the procedure. The patient subsequently achieved progressive hemodynamic stabilization. After prolonged mechanical ventilation and tracheostomy, neurological recovery was favorable. At discharge, echocardiography showed normal biventricular systolic function. This case illustrates that prompt escalation to rescue mechanical thrombectomy may be considered in selected patients with high-risk PE when shock, electrical instability, and right ventricular overload persist despite systemic thrombolysis.
title: Catastrophic High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Recurrent Cardiac Arrest Successfully Treated With Rescue Mechanical Thrombectomy After Systemic Thrombolysis.

abstract: Tirzepatide is a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist that produces substantial weight loss and improves multiple cardiometabolic risk factors. Current evidence supports its cardiovascular safety, with no established association between licensed tirzepatide therapy and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). As its clinical use continues to expand, reporting unusual cardiovascular presentations remains important for pharmacovigilance. We present a case of a 48-year-old South Asian man with obesity, diet-controlled prediabetes, a history of smoking, and a family history of premature coronary artery disease who had been receiving tirzepatide for approximately 18 months, achieving a weight loss of approximately 30 kg. Following increased physical activity, he developed progressive exertional chest pain and dyspnoea. Electrocardiography demonstrated inferolateral ischaemic changes, and serial high-sensitivity troponin T measurements were consistent with a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). Transthoracic echocardiography showed preserved left ventricular systolic function with inferior regional wall motion abnormalities. Coronary angiography revealed severe triple-vessel coronary artery disease involving the left anterior descending, left circumflex, and right coronary arteries. He subsequently underwent successful coronary artery bypass grafting with an uncomplicated postoperative recovery. Although a temporal association existed between prolonged tirzepatide therapy, substantial weight loss, and presentation with NSTEMI, the presence of advanced multivessel coronary artery disease suggests longstanding atherosclerosis rather than a direct adverse effect of tirzepatide. A more plausible explanation is that significant weight loss improved functional capacity, allowing increased physical activity that unmasked previously silent obstructive coronary artery disease. This interpretation is consistent with current evidence demonstrating favourable cardiovascular effects of tirzepatide while acknowledging that causality cannot be established from a single case. This case highlights the importance of thoroughly evaluating new exertional chest pain in patients receiving tirzepatide despite marked improvements in weight and metabolic health. Clinicians should remain vigilant for underlying coronary artery disease in individuals with traditional cardiovascular risk factors. This report describes a temporal association rather than a causal relationship and contributes to the growing body of real-world experience with tirzepatide.
title: Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction Following Significant Weight Loss During Tirzepatide Therapy: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in middle-aged adults. However, there is a lack of data on its clinical profile, cardiovascular risk factors, angiographic characteristics, management, and outcomes in armed forces personnel. Thus, this study was conducted to evaluate the clinical characteristics, risk factors, angiographic profile, treatment strategies, complications, and outcomes of ACS among paramilitary forces personnel.
METHODS: This study included 173 paramilitary forces personnel diagnosed with ACS. Demographic and service-related characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, clinical presentation, Killip class, laboratory and echocardiographic parameters, time to revascularization, coronary angiographic findings, treatment strategies, procedural complications, and clinical outcomes were evaluated.
RESULTS: The mean age of participants was 46.5±7.52 years, and 98.8% (n=171) were male. The most frequent cardiovascular risk factors were smoking (n=99, 57.2%) and hypertension (n=94, 54.3%), followed by dyslipidemia (n=58, 33.5%) and diabetes mellitus (n=49, 28.3%). Anterior wall myocardial infarction was the most common presentation (n=74, 42.8%), followed by inferior wall myocardial infarction (n=64, 36.99%) and non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (n=21, 12.1%). The mean ejection fraction was 45.6±7.49%, and regional wall motion abnormalities were seen in 76.9% (n=133) of patients. Pharmaco-invasive therapy was the preferred treatment strategy in 68.8% (n=119), with thrombolysis being done in 72.3% (n=125). Coronary angiography was performed in 88.4% (n=153) of cases. The most common angiographic finding was single-vessel disease (n=82, 53.6%), and the left anterior descending artery was the most frequently involved vessel (n=92, 61.7%). The majority (n=99, 78.0%) of patients who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) had a single stent. The most common electrical complications were complete heart block (n=8, 4.6%) and ventricular tachycardia (n=7, 4.0%). Conclusions: ACS in paramilitary forces personnel predominantly affected middle-aged men and was associated with a high prevalence of modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, especially smoking and hypertension. Main management strategies were pharmaco-invasive therapy and coronary intervention. Early identification of cardiovascular risk factors and prompt reperfusion may improve prognosis in this population.
title: Clinico-Angiographic Profile of Paramilitary Forces Personnel Presenting With Acute Coronary Syndrome at a Tertiary Care Institute in Jammu and Kashmir, India.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fulminant perimyocarditis is an uncommon cause of cardiogenic shock and refractory cardiac arrest. We describe Influenza A (H1N1)-associated perimyocarditis managed with a stepwise extracorporeal resuscitation strategy.
CASE: A 54-year-old woman presented with chest pain, hypoxemia, and cardiogenic shock. Electrocardiography (ECG) showed diffuse ST-segment elevation. Echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dysfunction and a fibrinous pericardial effusion and coronary angiography excluded obstructive disease. Despite vasoactive support and mechanical circulatory support with microaxial flow pump Impella CP (flow 2.7 L/min.), she deteriorated to Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) Stage E with pulseless electrical activity (PEA). During automated chest compressions, mechanical circulatory support with femoral Impella CP was rapidly escalated to venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Respiratory polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was positive for Influenza A (H1N1) virus. Antiviral therapy, heparin anticoagulation, ventilation, and organ support were instituted. Hemodynamics stabilized, lactate cleared, and neurological examination after decannulation was intact. Progressive myocardial recovery permitted VA-ECMO explant on Day 3 and Impella CP removal 24 h thereafter. She was extubated on Day 6 and discharged from intensive care unit (ICU) on Day 10. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging confirmed myocarditis; echocardiography at follow-up showed preserved biventricular function.
CONCLUSION: In fulminant perimyocarditis with refractory arrest, rapid activation of an extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) pathway with early VA-ECMO-combined with ventricular unloading-can bridge to myocardial recovery and favorable neurological outcome. Regional systems enabling safe transfer under continuous cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) are critical.

abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events.
RESULTS: For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSION: In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.
title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since its inception in the 1970s, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) has undergone significant advances. This review provides an updated perspective on PCI to assist general physicians in navigating various clinical presentations, determining the appropriate patient and optimal timing for intervention, as well as selecting appropriate devices for different populations.
METHODS: Clinical trials from a targeted three-stage PubMed search, focusing on PCI indications, procedural timing, and device selection, were analyzed and integrated with consensus guidelines from leading cardiology organizations.
RESULTS: For patients presenting with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), PCI is recommended within 12 h of the onset of symptoms, ideally achieving a door-to-balloon time of 90-120 min from the first medical contact. Beyond the 12 h mark, the procedure remains indicated for those exhibiting persistent ischemia, clinical symptoms, or complications such as shock, arrhythmia, or heart failure. In cases of non-STEMI (NSTEMI), patients generally benefit from PCI during their initial hospital stay, although an early invasive approach may not provide clinical advantages for frail elderly individuals. Complete revascularization is typically favored over treating only the culprit lesion, except in instances of cardiogenic shock. For those with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS), while PCI enhances quality of life and improves symptom management, most clinical trials report that it does not significantly reduce mortality or major cardiovascular incidents. The initial plain old balloon angioplasty faced complications of restenosis and acute vessel closure. While bare metal stents addressed acute closure, the problem of restenosis persisted and stent thrombosis was noted. Current drug-eluting stents (DESs) are the preferred choice owing to superior clinical outcomes, with lower restenosis and stent thrombosis rates. Although theoretically ideal, bioresorbable scaffolds (BRSs) are still undergoing further research since they have yet to prove superior to DESs in clinical trials. In addition, drug-coated balloons (DCBs) have become a specialized treatment, especially for managing in-stent restenosis.
CONCLUSION: The necessity for and timing of PCI are dictated by the patient's specific clinical presentation. Immediate intervention is critical for STEMI patients, within 12 h of onset, or those with complications, while NSTEMI cases should be treated during the hospital admission. For CCS, PCI serves as an elective option to alleviate symptoms without altering long-term survival. The DES remains the primary tool in modern PCI, with BRS still undergoing research trials and DCBs serving specialized roles.
title: A Practical Update on Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) for the General Physician, Answering Questions of Patient Type, Timing, and Device Choice.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Secondary mitral regurgitation (MR) contributes to morbidity and mortality in patients with symptomatic valve disease. Although transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is beneficial, many patients remain suboptimal candidates. Posterior leaflet restoration (PLR) provides a prosthetic coaptation surface via an adaptive coaptation element that inflates during systole and deflates during diastole to facilitate leaflet coaptation.
OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate the safety and feasibility of PLR using the MRace implant (Polares Medical, Inc).
METHODS: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant in Georgia and Brazil (EXPLORE MR) enrolled 78 symptomatic patients with severe secondary MR (≥3+), stratified post hoc by left ventricular end-diastolic volume: nonseverely enlarged left ventricle (NSELV) (N = 46) and severely enlarged left ventricle (SELV) (N = 32). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality; secondary endpoints were MR reduction and functional outcomes.
RESULTS: The implant was successfully deployed in 96.2% of patients. All-cause mortality at 30 days was 6.4%. MR ≤2+ was achieved in 93.8% of patients at 30 days and was sustained in 90.6% at 1 year. Patients with NSELV showed better results in MR ≤1+ at every time point (94.4% at 30 days, 89.5% at 1 year) compared with the SELV group (79.3% and 69.2%, respectively). The NSELV subgroup demonstrated better functional recovery, with NYHA functional class I or II rising from 8.7% to 84.2%, vs a more attenuated response in the SELV group (15.6%-76.9%). The 6-minute walk test improved in the paired NSELV cohort (Δ +93.9 m), but not in paired patients with SELV (Δ -7.8 m). Kaplan-Meier 1-year all-cause mortality was 29.5% overall and was better in patients with NSELV (19.4%) than in SELV (41.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: PLR with the MRace implant achieves substantial MR reduction and meaningful functional improvement, most pronounced in patients without severely enlarged left ventricles. (XPLORE MRace [BR]: Early Feasibility Experience of Posterior Leaflet Restoration to Reduce Mitral Regurgitation Using the MRace Implant [EXPLORE MRace]; NCT06113354).
title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual shunt is a known complication in percutaneous patent foramen ovale (PFO) closure, and moderate to large residual shunt has been associated with an increased risk of recurrent stroke. Device-related factors, such as device size, have been associated with residual shunt, but comparative data per device type are scarce.
AIMS: We compared the prevalence of moderate to large residual shunt at 6 months between the Amplatzer and Occlutech devices.
METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing successful percutaneous PFO closure with an Amplatzer or Occlutech dedicated closure device within the CAHAL centers Amsterdam UMC and Leiden UMC between 2018 and 2024 were included. The study population was divided into patients treated with an Occlutech and an Amplatzer device. The prevalence of moderate/large residual shunt at 6 months of follow-up was compared between the two groups. As a sensitivity analysis, a logistic regression was conducted to determine the association between the treatment groups and moderate/large residual shunt. The logistic regression was conducted in a weighted population using inverse probability weighting (IPTW), correcting for age, sex, smoking status, shunt size at baseline, device size, and atrial septal aneurysm.
RESULTS: A total of 413 patients were included with an average age of 45.8 ± 11.3 years and 51.6% were male. Of the included patients, 279 were treated with an Amplatzer- and 134 with an Occlutech device. In the group treated with an Amplatzer, 22.2% of the patients had a moderate or large residual shunt at 6 months compared to 14.9% in the Occlutech group (p = 0.11). The sensitivity analysis did not show an association between device type and moderate/large shunt OR 0.71 (95% CI: 0.39-1.28, p = 0.25).
CONCLUSION: In this study, no significant difference was observed in moderate/large residual shunt prevalence at 6 months of follow-up between the Occlutech and Amplatzer devices.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Residual Shunt at 6 Months Follow-up After Percutaneous Patent Foramen Ovale Closure in CAHAL: A Comparison of Occlutech and Amplatzer.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for 12 months is the current standard of care for patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Recent evidence indicates that potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT) after 1 to 3 months of DAPT following drug-eluting-stent (DES) implantation reduces major bleeding events without increasing the risk of major ischemic outcomes in patients with acute coronary syndrome. However, the optimal timing of aspirin discontinuation in STEMI patients treated with P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT remains uncertain.
DESIGN: STARS DAPT is an investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, open-label, precision-based, randomized controlled pilot trial with a blinded outcome assessment. Patients with STEMI who underwent successful primary PCI of the culprit lesion with a newer-generation polymer-free DES will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to potent P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT (with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge) for 12 months vs. standard DAPT for 12 months. The primary efficacy endpoint is the rate of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), defined as the composite of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial re-infarction, non-fatal stroke, urgent target vessel revascularization, or definite/probable stent thrombosis, at 12 months. The primary safety endpoint is Bleeding Academic Research Consortium (BARC) class 3 or 5 major bleeding at 12 months. The study is designed to provide estimates of treatment effects and their precision to inform the design of a subsequent larger randomized trial.
ENROLMENT STATUS: The trial aims to recruit a total of 350 patients. The first patient was enrolled on December 1, 2025.
CONCLUSION: STARS DAPT is a randomized pilot study assessing the safety and efficacy of a potent oral P2Y12 inhibitor-based SAPT strategy, with aspirin discontinued after an initial period of DAPT during the index hospitalization and before hospital discharge, following primary PCI with a newer-generation polymer-free DES in patients with STEMI. The findings will inform future large-scale trial design and may help optimize antiplatelet strategies and guide clinical decision-making after primary PCI.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov: Identifier, NCT05785897.
FUNDING SOURCE: Unrestricted research grant from Concept Medical (Tampa, FL, USA) to Geneva University Hospitals, Switzerland.
title: Potent P2Y12 inhibitor monotherapy versus dual antiplatelet therapy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention: Rationale and design of the STARS DAPT randomized pilot trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiogenic shock (CS) severity is defined by the Society for Cardiovascular Angiography and Interventions (SCAI) stages and modifications from the Cardiogenic Shock Working Group (CSWG). Lactate thresholds, treatment intensity, and cardiac arrest modifiers remain incompletely defined. We aimed to refine the 2022 CSWG staging criteria using contemporary data.
METHODS: Patients with CS from heart failure (HF-CS) or myocardial infarction (MI-CS) enrolled in the multicenter CSWG registry (2021-2025) were analyzed. Associations between systolic blood pressure (SBP), lactate, treatment intensity, and in-hospital mortality, which is considered a surrogate for CS severity, were examined. External application of the updated system was performed in an independent U.S. health system.
RESULTS: Among 11,640 patients (60.5% HF-CS, 26.1% MI-CS), SBP and lactate demonstrated graded relationships with mortality across thresholds (SBP<60, 60-<90, ≥90 mmHg; lactate 0-2, >2-5, >5-10, >10 mmol/L). Mortality increased incrementally with treatment intensity. The 2026 staging system incorporating these thresholds and the number of vasoactive drugs and temporary mechanical circulatory support devices (stage C: 1-2, D: 3-4, E: ≥5) demonstrated progressive mortality across stages. Compared with prior CSWG staging, 28.4% of stage D and 56.4% of stage E patients were reclassified, with lower mortality among those reclassified to less severe stages. Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest functioned best as a stage modifier, whereas in-hospital cardiac arrest corresponded to stage E. Findings were consistent across HF-CS and MI-CS. The 2026 CS staging system was evaluated in 1,417,637 patients in a geographically and structurally diverse healthcare system and demonstrated a graded, monotonic increase in mortality across stages A-E.
CONCLUSIONS: Using fewer clinical variables, the 2026 CSWG criteria provide a simple framework for CS severity staging that is applicable among HF-CS and MI-CS patients, and can be standardized across clinical trials and healthcare settings.

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry analysis from the multicentre CSWG registry (2021-2025) with external application in an independent U.S. health system; 11,640 patients (60.5% HF-CS, 26.1% MI-CS) and 1,417,637 patients in the external system.
appraisal.main_limitation: In-hospital mortality is used as a surrogate for severity and the staging has not been tested for guiding treatment.
appraisal.one_line: Refined cardiogenic shock staging that adds lactate, systolic pressure, vasoactive drug count and support devices, applied in HF-CS and MI-CS.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Mortality increased incrementally with treatment intensity. Compared with prior CSWG staging, 28.4% of stage D and 56.4% of stage E patients were reclassified, with lower mortality among those reclassified to less severe stages. The 2026 CS staging system demonstrated a graded, monotonic increase in mortality across stages A-E.
appraisal.why_it_matters: A simpler shared severity definition could standardise enrolment and stratification in shock trials.

title: Updated Staging System to Define Cardiogenic Shock Severity A Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Report.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included.
EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores.
RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicentre registry cohort (NL-CFT) in 4 clinical centres; 553 patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months.
appraisal.main_limitation: Mostly female cohort with a composite dominated by soft events and limited power for hard outcomes.
appraisal.one_line: Continuous thermodilution microvascular resistance reserve did not predict clinical events in angina with non-obstructive coronary arteries, though it tracked angina at follow-up.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Questions the prognostic value of an increasingly used invasive microvascular index and informs coronary function testing.

title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.

abstract: The recurrence of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) can be reduced through healthy lifestyle modification; however, many survivors struggle to sustain behavioral changes after hospital discharge. Previous studies have primarily focused on biomedical and behavioral outcomes, with limited attention to the psychosocial, emotional, and cultural processes involved in long-term recovery. This study explored the lived experiences of ACS survivors as they adapted to lifestyle changes within their social and cultural contexts. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 15 ACS survivors between three months and one year after the cardiac event and analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Three interconnected themes emerged: (1) creating new habits, (2) reconciling with the situation, and (3) the dual role of family. Lifestyle modification was experienced as a continuous struggle involving deeply rooted habits, emotional dependence, declining motivation, and the process of self-acceptance in seeking inner peace. Some participants gradually developed self-regulation and adaptive coping strategies, whereas others remained trapped in smoking behaviors, emotional distress, and hopelessness. Participants perceived psychosocial support from healthcare professionals as limited and expressed a need for greater emotional reassurance and coping assistance. Psychospiritual adaptation was shaped by the Javanese values of nrimo and ikhlas. These values helped participants accept physical limitations, reduce fear, and reconstruct meaning after illness. Family relationships served both as sources of support and stress, while patriarchal family dynamics sometimes hindered open communication. These findings suggest that recovery after ACS involves identity reconstruction, emotional regulation, and culturally embedded coping processes that extend beyond medical adherence alone.
title: From Surviving to Thriving: ACS Survivors' Experiences in Lifestyle Transformation to Prevent Recurrence-A Qualitative Study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests that inflammatory and nutritional status play key roles in the prognosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVD). The Inflammatory Prognostic Index (IPI), integrating both inflammatory and nutritional metrics, has been linked to multiple subtypes of coronary artery disease (CAD). However, the association between IPI and long-term prognosis in patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO) after successful PCI remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the prognostic role of IPI in patients with CTO who underwent successful PCI.
METHODS: A total of 525 patients with CTO who underwent successful PCI were enrolled in this study. Participants were stratified into a MACE group and a control group, as well as three subgroups (T1, T2, T3) by IPI tertiles. Baseline characteristics were compared, and Cox regression analysis were performed. The receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) was used to determine the predictive value of IPI for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE).
RESULTS: A total of 76 patients with 82 MACE were recorded during the follow-up. Patients with MACE exhibited significantly higher C-reactive protein (CRP) and IPI levels (p < 0.05). Patients in T3 (high IPI group) had higher white blood cell count, neutrophil count, CRP, creatinine, and IPI, while they had lower lymphocyte count, albumin (ALB), and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) (p < 0.05). In addition, patients in the highest IPI tertile exhibited a higher risk of target vessel revascularization (TVR) and composite MACE (p < 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that IPI was an independent predictor of MACE in patients with CTO who underwent successful PCI (p < 0.05). Moreover, patients in the highest IPI tertile had a 2.484-fold higher risk of MACE (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: IPI may serve as a supplementary prognostic tool due to its simplicity and low cost. However, given its modest predictive performance, it should be combined with existing risk models to improve predictive value and facilitate clinical decision-making.
title: The prognostic value of inflammatory prognostic index in patients with chronic total occlusion undergoing successful PCI: a single-center prospective cohort study.

abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) induces persistent neuroinflammation and white matter injury that limit neurological recovery, yet effective repair-oriented therapies remain lacking. Although microbiota influences stroke outcomes, how microbial activity drives central nervous system repair is unclear. Here, we integrate clinical microbiome profiling, experimental stroke models, multi-omics analyses, and mechanistic validation to define a microbiota-metabolite-glial signaling axis that promotes post-stroke recovery. Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk) is associated with favorable outcomes in patients and improves recovery in mice without altering infarct size, supporting a repair-promoting rather than neuroprotective mechanism. Mechanistically, Akk increases circulating isorhamnetin (Iso), a key systemic mediator that suppresses lipid-laden, pro-inflammatory microglia and promotes oligodendrocyte maturation and white matter repair. Iso reprograms microglia to secrete PSAP, and conditioned medium-but not direct Iso-activates GPR37-ERK signaling in oligodendrocytes. In vitro knockdown of Psap or Gpr37 markedly attenuates these effects, demonstrating a microglia-dependent mechanism. In vivo adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated Gpr37 knockdown abolishes the beneficial effects of Akk and Iso on functional recovery and white matter repair, establishing the necessity of PSAP-GPR37 signaling. These findings identify a microbiota-driven metabolic pathway linking gut activity to white matter repair after IS.
title: A microbiota-metabolite-glial axis drives white matter repair via isorhamnetin-PSAP-GPR37 signaling after ischemic stroke.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable-polymer sirolimus-eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM.
AIMS: In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5-year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus-eluting stent (EES).
METHODS: TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non-stratified outcomes in DM versus non-DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia-driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis.
RESULTS: Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non-DM patients, TLF (p < 0.001), cardiac death (p < 0.001), TVMI (p = 0.002), ischemia-driven TLR (p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis (p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM.
CONCLUSION: This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Final 5-Year Results of Abluminal Groove-Filled Biodegradable-Polymer Sirolimus-Eluting Stent Versus Durable-Polymer Everolimus-Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dual-lumen microcatheters (DLMs) are adjunctive devices that has been increasingly incorporated into contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). These catheters contain two independent working lumens, a rapid-exchange (RX) port and an over-the-wire (OTW) port, within a single low-profile shaft, permitting guidewire advancement and exchange within a shared working space. Published consensus documents have focused predominantly on chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions, with less on non-CTO lesions.
METHODS: This narrative review describes five practical applications of DLMs in non-CTO lesions. For each technique, we outlined the procedural rationale, a stepwise approach, and technical considerations.
RESULTS: Five applications are presented: (1) aorto-ostial wiring in the setting of a protruding ostial stent or anomalous coronary takeoff; (2) reverse wiring of a side branch with an acute or angulated takeoff; (3) side-branch re-entry after stent deployment; (4) contrast injection through the OTW port; and (5) parallel wiring for complex lesions.
CONCLUSIONS: DLMs offer several practical applications beyond CTO PCI. Familiarity with these techniques and their technical considerations may help operators select and apply DLM-assisted strategies in complex non-CTO lesions.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Dual-Lumen Microcatheters in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Five Useful Techniques to Facilitate Coronary Wiring in Non-CTO Lesions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Preserving internal iliac artery (IIA) patency during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for aortobiiliac aneurysms typically requires substantial contrast volume, posing risk to patients with renal insufficiency.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We present the case of an elderly female with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3b (baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate 35 mL/min/1.73 m², serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL) and an aortobiiliac aneurysm who underwent complex bilateral iliac side-branch (iliac branch endoprosthesis [IBE]) deployment. The procedure used intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) as the primary guidance to minimize contrast exposure. A notable intraoperative challenge arose on the left side, where retrograde cannulation was unsuccessful due to anatomical tortuosity and sheath dislodgement. We therefore performed a left axillary cut-down, which facilitated successful IIA reconstruction and resolved a type 1b endoleak. The total contrast volume employed was approximately 38 mL. Incidental findings included hyperthyroidism and suspected lymphoproliferative disorder.
CONCLUSION: Intravascular ultrasound-guided bilateral IBE is feasible and substantially reduces contrast exposure in patients with renal impairment, though technical flexibility is essential for complex anatomy.Clinical ImpactIVUS-guided bilateral iliac branch endoprosthesis deployment may offer a contrast-sparing option for patients with chronic kidney disease undergoing endovascular repair of complex aortobiiliac aneurysms. Using IVUS for vessel identification, sizing, landing-zone selection, and stent-apposition assessment can reduce reliance on iodinated contrast while preserving internal iliac artery perfusion. This case shows that bilateral reconstruction is feasible with only 38 mL of contrast, even when complex anatomy requires axillary access. Its innovation is using IVUS as the primary guidance modality, with angiography reserved for confirmation and troubleshooting.
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
title: Bilateral Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Deployment With IVUS-Guided Contrast-Sparing Technique: A Complex Case Report.

abstract: Pulmonary tumor embolism (PTE) is a rare but potentially life-threatening form of non-thrombotic pulmonary embolism. Despite advancements in management, it remains a challenging entity due to its unpredictable clinical course and high mortality rate. With the advent of minimally invasive endovascular treatment modalities, the management of pulmonary embolism has witnessed a shift from systemic thrombolysis or surgical thromboarterectomy to catheter-directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy, or pharmaco-mechanical thrombectomy, combining mechanical thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis. We report a rare case of intermediate-risk pulmonary tumor embolism managed by large-bore aspiration thrombectomy.
title: Mechanical Thrombectomy for Pulmonary Tumor Embolism Masquerading as Bland Pulmonary Embolism: A Case Report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between changes in paravalvular leakage (PVL) and serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is unexplored. We aimed to investigate the short-term changes in PVL after TAVI and their association with LDH elevation.
METHODS: A total of 550 consecutive patients underwent TAVI from 2020 to 2024. Of these, 313 receiving SAPIEN 3 (S3) or SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA (S3UR) valves were included in this study. Patients were categorized into two groups based on whether their PVL severity worsened by at least one grade from immediately after the procedure to hospital discharge.
RESULTS: PVL deterioration was observed in 16.3% of patients. The incidence of moderate or greater LDH elevation was significantly higher in the PVL deterioration group than in the non-PVL deterioration group at 7 days (17.6% vs. 8.4%; P = 0.04) and 1 month (29.4% vs. 8.8%; P < 0.01) after the procedure. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for predicting PVL deterioration using the sizing index (SI) was 0.84, with an optimal cut-off value of 96.5% (odds ratio (OR): 13.6; 95% confidence interval (CI): 6.55-31.1; P < 0.01). Multivariable analysis showed that an aortic valve calcium score ≥ 1,435, use of the S3UR valve, and an SI < 96.5 were independently associated with PVL deterioration.
CONCLUSION: Early PVL deterioration after TAVI with a balloon-expandable valve may be associated with LDH elevation. These findings highlight the importance of selecting a prosthetic valve with an appropriate sizing ratio to minimize PVL deterioration after TAVI.
title: Association Between Changes in Paravalvular Leakage After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation and Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase.

abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is a rare but increasingly recognized cause of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and sudden cardiac death. It has been associated with several predisposing factors, including hormone replacement therapy, autoimmune disorders, fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD), connective tissue diseases, atherosclerosis, migraine, pregnancy, and the postpartum period. SCAD most commonly affects young to middle-aged women who present with acute myocardial infarction (MI) despite the absence of traditional atherosclerotic risk factors. Coronary angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosis, allowing visualization of the characteristic dissection patterns within the coronary vessel wall. Management is typically conservative as spontaneous healing of the dissection is common; however, revascularization with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) may be necessary in patients with hemodynamic instability, ongoing ischemia, or failure of medical therapy.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Right ventricular infarction (RVI) is commonly observed in patients with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction and typically results from proximal right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. However, the occurrence of RVI and its clinical characteristics in patients with distal RCA lesions are not well defined.
METHODS: We retrospectively investigated 128 patients with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction caused by RCA occlusion who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention at our institution between January 2020 and December 2023. RVI was diagnosed based on echocardiographic evidence and hemodynamic instability. Clinical characteristics and incidence rates were compared between patients with RVI [the RVI (+) group] and those without RVI [the RVI (-) group]. Findings on coronary angiography were assessed in detail for patients with distal RCA lesions.
RESULTS: RVI was identified in 24/128 patients (18.8%), including 3/31 patients (9.7%) with distal RCA lesions. Right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly lower in the RVI (+) group (-14.0% [-16.4, -11.6] vs. -16.4% [-18.7, -13.9]; p=0.004), as was right ventricular free wall strain (RVFWS) (-14.7% [-18.5, -10.6] vs. -17.7% [-20.7, -15.0]; p=0.01). RVGLS and RVFWS values were comparable in the RVI (+) group regardless of whether the RCA lesion was distal or proximal. There was no significant difference in TIMI flow before or after percutaneous coronary intervention or in the distribution of lesions.
CONCLUSIONS: RVI can be caused by distal RCA lesions, albeit less often than by proximal RCA lesions. No significant differences in RV strain parameters were observed between distal and proximal lesions.
title: Right ventricular infarction with a culprit lesion in the distal right coronary artery: incidence and clinical characteristics.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: NT-proBNP is the gold-standard biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring congestive heart failure (CHF); however, its role in detecting atrial fibrillation (AFib) is gaining attention. This study assessed the influence of aberrant cardiac rhythms on plasma NT-proBNP (pNT) considering urinary NT-proBNP (uNT) as a noninvasive alternative in selected clinical scenarios.
METHODS: In 824 patients presenting with chest pain at the emergency department of the University Hospital of Regensburg, pNT was assessed. A subset of 355 patients additionally provided uNT.
RESULTS: Both pNT and uNT were significantly increased in AFib, and lesser in atrial flutter (AFlut) and right ventricular (RV) pacing compared to SR (each p < 0.05). A pNT cutoff of 900 pg/mL yielded 74% sensitivity and 83% specificity for discriminating AFib from SR (AUC = 0.85). In multivariate regression, pNT or uNT and history of AFib were independent predictors of AFib (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Both pNT and uNT are significantly elevated in AFib, and to a lesser extent AFlut, and RV pacing independently of heart failure. These findings align with prior observations and provide further evidence supporting adequately powered prospective studies to evaluate rhythm-adjusted diagnostic thresholds for CHF in AFib. In addition, uNT may complement pNT when venous access is difficult or serial remote monitoring is required.
title: Blood and urinary NT-proBNP: atrial fibrillation-associated patterns and cardiac dysfunction in acute chest pain.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Statin intolerance may disrupt lipid-lowering therapy (LLT). We characterized clinician-documented intolerance and assessed whether cardiovascular risk was concentrated among patients who discontinued all LLT.
METHODS: We studied new statin users at Mass General Brigham using medication records dated 1987 through November 2025. Temporal trend analyses were restricted to 2001 through 2024. We characterized postintolerance management and examined cardiovascular outcomes using time-varying Cox models. Within the intolerance cohort, we compared patients who discontinued all LLT with those who continued any LLT.
RESULTS: Among 254 035 new statin users, 10 644 (4.2%) developed documented intolerance after a median of 3.1 years. Musculoskeletal symptoms were documented in 68.1%. Within 90 days, 39.9% discontinued all LLT and fewer than 10% received a nonstatin-based strategy. At 3 to 6 months, mean low-density lipoprotein cholesterol increased by 6.8 mg/dL among discontinuers and decreased by 4.9 mg/dL among continuers. Compared with statin-tolerant patients, intolerance was associated with higher risks of coronary artery bypass grafting, percutaneous coronary intervention, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke (hazard ratios, 1.12-1.55). Within the intolerance cohort, discontinuing all LLT was associated with higher risk across all outcomes, with hazard ratios ranging from 1.38 for mortality to 2.14 for venous thromboembolism.
CONCLUSIONS: Clinician-documented statin intolerance was frequently followed by complete LLT discontinuation and limited use of nonstatin therapy. Complete discontinuation identified a high-risk subgroup with worsening lipid trajectories, supporting systematic reassessment and restoration of statin or nonstatin therapy.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Door-to-balloon (DTB) time is a key performance metric in the management of ST-elevation myocardial infarction, with shorter times strongly associated with improved myocardial salvage and reduced mortality. International cardiology guidelines recommend achieving DTB within 90 minutes for patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention. This quality improvement (QI) initiative aimed to identify determinants of delayed DTB time in a tertiary care hospital and implement structured system-level interventions.
METHODS: Root-cause analysis revealed delays related to financial clearance processes, off-hour Cath lab staffing, concurrent laboratory use, and delayed arrival of consultants and anesthesiologists. Interventions included workflow standardization, staff duty rosters, night supervision protocols, and real-time communication channels linking emergency, cardiology, Cath lab, and administrative teams. Monthly DTB times were monitored from September 2022 to December 2025.
RESULTS: Median DTB times exceeded 100 min during the baseline period (101-111 min) but decreased to 69-84.6 min following implementation of the QI interventions. Achievement of the recommended DTB target (<90 min) became more consistent throughout the postintervention period.
CONCLUSION: A structured multidisciplinary QI strategy focusing on financial workflow reform, staffing readiness, and real-time interdepartmental communication was associated with substantial and sustained reductions in DTB time at a tertiary care center. Continuous monitoring, protocol reinforcement, and adaptive process refinement were essential to maintaining performance near internationally recommended targets.
title: Optimizing Door-to-Balloon Time in STEMI Care through Structured Quality Improvement at a Tertiary Centre.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic heart disease remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with platelet activation playing a crucial role in its pathogenesis. Platelet indices such as mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), platelet-large cell ratio (P-LCR), and plateletcrit (PCT) are increasingly recognized as simple and cost-effective markers of platelet activity and thrombotic risk.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This hospital-based cross-sectional study included 180 participants divided into three groups: chronic stable angina (CSA), acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and healthy controls (60 each). Platelet count and platelet volume indices were measured using an automated hematology analyzer, and statistical analysis was performed to compare differences among groups.
RESULTS: Platelet count was significantly lower in the ACS group compared to CSA and controls. In contrast, MPV, PDW, P-LCR, and PCT were significantly elevated in ACS, reflecting increased platelet activation. MPV emerged as an independent predictor of ischemic heart disease. Among all parameters, P-LCR and MPV demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy. Platelet indices also showed association with cardiovascular risk factors and disease severity.
CONCLUSION: Platelet volume indices, particularly MPV and P-LCR, are reliable and easily accessible markers of platelet activation in ischemic heart disease. They may serve as useful adjuncts in diagnosis and risk stratification in both stable and acute coronary conditions.
title: Role of Platelet Count and Platelet Volume Indices in Ischemic Heart Disease: An Observational Comparative Study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The degree of tricuspid regurgitation (TR) is related to mortality. The majority of TR is secondary, and surgery consists mainly of annuloplasty repair (TVr), but repair durability is a prerequisite for a lasting treatment effect. We performed a systematic assessment of TVr durability.
METHODS: A systematic literature search was performed (MEDLINE, Cochrane Library and Web of Science). Follow-up of TVr techniques and TR recurrence rates were used to estimate incidence rates which were then meta-analyzed using a single-arm meta-analysis model with random-effects. Comparisons between techniques were performed to obtain incidence rate ratios (IRR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05.
RESULTS: A total of 50 studies met the criteria for inclusion (5 randomized and 45 observational), with 15,563 patients, representing 79,763 patient-years (mean follow-up: 3.9 years). Overall recurrence rate was 2.73 per 100 person-years (95% CI 2.15-3.47). Ring annuloplasty had lowest rates (1.81; 95% CI 1.17-2.79), followed by band (2.58; 95% CI 1.66-4.00) and suture (4.06; 95% CI 2.93-5.64). There was a large difference in treatment effects within and between groups (P for interaction=0.011). Compared to suture, ring annuloplasty was associated with lower TR recurrence (IRR 0.45; P = 0.003), but not versus band (IRR 0.71; P = 0.26). There was no difference between band and suture (IRR 0.63; P = 0.12).
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term durability of TVr techniques is extremely heterogeneous. We identified the use of rigid rings and flexible bands as being associated with lower recurrence rates compared to suture techniques.
title: Tricuspid valve repair: A systematic review and meta-analysis of different surgical techniques and their long-term results.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the United States, with in-stent restenosis (ISR) posing a significant challenge following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Drug-eluting stents (DES) have been widely used to mitigate ISR; however, until recently, no drug-coated balloon (DCB) catheter had been approved for use in the United States. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has now approved AGENT DCB, a paclitaxel-coated balloon catheter, offering a novel approach to treating ISR.
HYPOTHESIS: The approval of AGENT DCB represents a pivotal advancement in PCI, providing an effective alternative to traditional balloon angioplasty for ISR.
METHODS: This article is an editorial review and does not involve original research, statistical analysis, or software-based evaluations. The findings and discussion are based on the results of the AGENT IDE trial and related literature on the efficacy of DCB catheters in the treatment of ISR.
RESULTS: The AGENT IDE trial, a randomized, multicenter study involving 600 participants across 40 US sites, demonstrated that the paclitaxel-coated balloon group had a significantly lower target lesion failure rate at 12 months compared to the uncoated balloon group (17.9% vs. 28.6%, p = 0.003). The reduction was primarily driven by a lower incidence of target lesion revascularization (13.0% vs. 24.7%, p = 0.001) and myocardial infarction related to the target vessel (5.8% vs. 11.1%, p = 0.02). Additionally, no cases of stent thrombosis were observed in the DCB group compared to 3.2% in the control group (p = 0.001), reinforcing the device's safety and efficacy.
CONCLUSIONS: The FDA approval of AGENT DCB marks a significant milestone in the management of ISR, offering a promising alternative to conventional interventions. With its ability to deliver antiproliferative therapy while avoiding the complications associated with permanent stents, DCB may revolutionize PCI strategies in the United States. Further studies assessing the long-term impact of this technology, as well as its application in broader patient populations, will be essential to solidify its role in clinical practice.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Two methods are used to determine cardiac troponin (cTn) thresholds for high-risk stratification for myocardial infarction (MI), namely the assay's healthy population 99th percentiles and a threshold that has a positive predictive value (PPV) of about 70%. We hypothesized that these methods may produce inconsistent prediction of MI risk.
METHODS: We compared the positive likelihood ratio (LR+), sensitivity, and specificity at 99th percentiles and published high-risk thresholds for a high-sensitivity (hs) cTnI (Abbott) and cTnT (Roche) assay. We simulated the high-risk threshold derivation methodology that derives thresholds with 70% PPV as a function of prevalence and sample size. We derived and validated thresholds based on LR+ = 20 and specificity = 95%.
RESULTS: In 2584 patients there was an almost 2-fold difference in LR+ between males and females at the sex-specific 99th percentiles, and a 2- to 3-fold difference between assays. Thresholds giving 70% PPV were much higher in lower-prevalence cohorts for both assays, being 3- to 10-fold lower at 5% than 20% prevalence. Thresholds derived using a LR+ or specificity had similar performance in a validation cohort between sexes but had a 2-fold difference in LR+ in a validation cohort between assays.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients presenting to the emergency department with possible MI, sex-specific 99th percentile thresholds convey lower risk of MI for females than males. Risks also differed between assays. Risk thresholds derived using the PPV vary considerably with the prevalence and size of cohort. Thresholds derived with specificity or positive likelihood ratio had more consistent risk-prediction.
title: Troponin Thresholds for Risk Stratification of Chest Pain Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department: Alternatives to the 99th Percentile.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate current clinical practice patterns and perceptions regarding steroid-eluting sinus implants (SESIs) among Italian rhinologists.
METHODS: A nationwide survey on SESIs use in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS) was developed by an advisory board of 5 Italian experts from tertiary referral centres and distributed to rhinology surgeons across Italy. Of 145 invited physicians, 103 responded (71%). Three respondents without experience or interest in SESIs were excluded, leaving 100 participants for analysis.
RESULTS: Among respondents, 46% were SESI Users and 54% Non-Users. SESIs were mainly used in revision ESS, frontal sinus surgery, and in patients with contraindications to systemic corticosteroids. Users valued SESIs for reducing restenosis and promoting controlled healing. In frontal sinus surgery, SESIs were commonly recommended in revision cases, especially for scarring-related restenosis. In ethmoid surgery, middle turbinate preservation influenced recommendations. Non-users cited high costs, lack of reimbursement, and limited guideline clarity as the main barriers.
CONCLUSIONS: This survey shows marked variability in SESI adoption in Italy. While benefits are acknowledged in selected cases, economic and guideline-related issues limit wider use, highlighting the need for cost-effectiveness studies and national guidelines to better define the role of SESIs in ESS.
journal: Acta otorhinolaryngologica Italica : organo ufficiale della Societa italiana di otorinolaringologia e chirurgia cervico-facciale
title: Steroid-eluting sinus implants in endoscopic sinus surgery: results of an Italian Nationwide Survey.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Brain-derived tau (BD-tau) selectively quantifies tau of central nervous system origin in blood and has demonstrated strong correlations with infarct volume and functional outcome in general ischaemic stroke, but data in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) are lacking.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: In a prospectively collected cohort of 101 lacunar stroke patients with an MRI-confirmed recent small subcortical infarct (RSSI) and 47 controls, we measured serum BD-tau using the HD-X SIMOA platform at baseline and 3 and 15 months after stroke. We examined associations of BD-tau with infarct size, chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (white matter hyperintensities [WMHs], lacunes, microbleeds, total SVD score), CSVD progression on follow-up MRI and functional outcome.
RESULTS: Baseline serum BD-tau was higher in RSSI patients than controls (median 9.54 [7.32-12.20] vs 7.75 [6.18-9.44] pg/mL; P = .003) and correlated with infarct diameter (rs = 0.222, P = 0.039). Brain-derived tau did not correlate with time from stroke symptom onset to blood sampling (rs = 0.150, P = .179). Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features (WMHs, lacunes, microbleeds, SVD score; all P > .05) at any timepoint. Longitudinally, BD-tau returned to control levels by 3 months (P = .374) and remained stable at 15 months (P = .985). Brain-derived tau was neither associated with new vascular MRI lesions on follow-up nor functional neurological outcome.
CONCLUSION: Serum BD-tau is elevated acutely in CSVD-related RSSI, correlates with infarct size and normalises by 3 months. Brain-derived tau was not associated with chronic CSVD neuroimaging features or disease progression, suggesting sensitivity to acute neuronal injury rather than chronic or progressive CSVD.
title: Serum brain-derived tau in lacunar stroke and cerebral small vessel disease.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.
RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.
CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe coronary calcification complicates percutaneous coronary intervention by limiting lesion compliance and impairing stent expansion.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the SonicForce Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy System (Abbott Vascular) in severely calcified de novo coronary lesions.
METHODS: TECTONIC CAD intravascular lithotripsy investigational device exemption (NCT06885177) was a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study of 335 patients at 40 U.S.
CENTERS: The primary safety endpoint was 30-day target lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically driven target lesion revascularization. The primary effectiveness endpoint was procedural success. Each endpoint was tested against a prespecified performance goal. A prespecified optical coherence tomography (OCT) substudy evaluated calcium modification and stent expansion.
RESULTS: A total of 335 patients were included in the full analysis set, with 330 and 334 as the evaluable populations for the primary safety and primary effectiveness endpoints, respectively, and a median follow-up duration of 36 days (Q1-Q3: 28-37 days). Thirty-day target lesion failure was 0.3% (1 of 330; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 0.0%-1.7%); the upper 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 1.7%, below the 12.9% performance goal (P < 0.0001). Procedural success was 97.0% (324 of 334; exact 2-sided 95% CI: 94.6%-98.6%); the lower 1-sided 97.5% confidence bound was 94.6%, above the 87.1% performance goal (P < 0.0001). In the OCT substudy, mean calcium length was 22.2 ± 10.3 mm, and the maximum contiguous calcium site had a calcium arc of 247.3 ± 99.0° and a thickness of 0.90 ± 0.25 mm at baseline. At this site, final stent area was 7.1 ± 1.9 mm2, with stent expansion of 95.9% ± 18.6%. Calcium fracture was identified in 62.5% (50 of 80) of lesions after intravascular lithotripsy and 66.3% (53 of 80) after stenting.
CONCLUSIONS: TECTONIC CAD met both prespecified coprimary safety and effectiveness endpoints, demonstrating low 30-day target lesion failure and high procedural success. OCT demonstrated calcium fracture and favorable stent expansion at maximum contiguous calcium.
